question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the Pythagorean identity

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta -{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Setting $\theta =5x-\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{cosh}^{2}⁡(5x-\frac{\pi }{4})-{sinh}^{2}⁡(5x-\frac{\pi }{4}) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2{cosh}^{2}⁡(5x-\frac{\pi }{4})+4{x}^{3}-2{sinh}^{2}⁡(5x-\frac{\pi }{4}))\,\text{d}x & =\int (2[{cosh}^{2}⁡(5x-\frac{\pi }{4})-{sinh}^{2}⁡(5x-\frac{\pi }{4})]+4{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (2+4{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 2\cdot \text{d}x+\int 4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x+{x}^{4}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
